title: What’s News in Markets: Anthropic IPO, Nvidia Drama, ‘GTA VI’

summary.headline: Anthropic IPO sparks AI hype, Nvidia slides after CEO scandal, GTA VI launch dampens Take-Two
summary.tldr: The week saw the S&P 500, Dow and Nasdaq slip into correction territory as AI stocks cooled. Anthropic’s debut IPO rose 17% then fell 8.5% below $89, while Nvidia’s shares dropped 23% after its CEO’s resignation and a board rebuff. Meanwhile, GTA VI launched to strong sales expectations but Take-Two’s stock fell 8% for the week.

key_points.point: The S&P 500 fell nearly 9%, the Dow dropped 10%, and the Nasdaq tumbled 8%, pushing all three into correction (a 10%+ decline from recent peaks).
key_points.why_it_matters: A correction signals broader market weakness and can affect portfolio values across sectors.

key_points.point: Anthropic went public at $83 per share, jumped over 30% intraday, closed up 17%, then slipped 8.5% to just under $89 on day two.
key_points.why_it_matters: The volatile debut shows how quickly investor sentiment can shift for AI companies amid sector backlash.

key_points.point: Nvidia’s board rejected calls to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang after his resignation over a sex and spy scandal; interim CEO Colette Kress led the earnings call.
key_points.why_it_matters: Leadership turmoil adds uncertainty to a company that had been the largest U.S. firm, influencing its stock performance.

key_points.point: Nvidia reported another quarter of strong revenue growth, beating forecasts, yet its shares fell 23% for the week, representing its worst weekly drop.
key_points.why_it_matters: Even solid earnings can’t offset market concerns about governance and regulatory pressure on chip exports.

key_points.point: Grand Theft Auto VI is expected to sell >30 million copies at $80+ each, but Take-Two Interactive’s shares fell nearly 4% on launch day and ended the week 8% lower.
key_points.why_it_matters: Big product launches don’t always translate into immediate stock gains, especially when broader market sentiment is negative.

numbers.context: Anthropic stock finish up on day one
Anthropic drop to just under $89 on day two

summary.lesson: When a company’s valuation hinges on a single charismatic leader, any leadership controversy can trigger a sharp stock decline (key-person risk); boards that quickly install stable interim leadership can help steady the company but may not fully offset market fear.
opinions_and_predictions: Jensen Huang’s allies campaigned for his return as CEO, but the board isn’t interested (report).
Interim CEO Colette Kress gave an assuring message that “we’ve got this,” but Wall Street remains skeptical (report).
Analysts noted that the Nvidia share slide is the worst weekly drop, implying heightened risk for the chip sector (report).

glossary.definition: A market decline of 10% or more from a recent high, indicating a pullback in prices.
glossary.example: The S&P 500 fell nearly 9% and the Dow dropped 10%, pushing both into correction territory.

glossary.definition: Initial public offering – the first time a private company sells shares to the public.
glossary.example: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share and saw the stock rise 17% on day one.

glossary.definition: The risk that a company’s performance is overly dependent on one individual’s leadership or reputation.
glossary.example: Nvidia’s stock fell sharply after CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid scandal.

glossary.definition: A temporary chief executive appointed to lead a company until a permanent CEO is selected.
glossary.example: Colette Kress served as interim CEO of Nvidia during the earnings call.

glossary.definition: Investors or early supporters who provide capital to a company before it goes public.
glossary.example: Anthropic’s early backers are making eye-popping profits after the IPO.

summary.quality_note: WSJ reporter Vicky Ge Huang presents market moves with data from index performance, company filings and earnings releases; statements are backed by reported numbers.
